Penultimate

/pih-NUHL-tuh-muht/ - the stress falls on NUHL · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Penultimate means next to last.

In the spelling bee's penultimate round, four of the five remaining spellers went out on the same silent "p."

Worked Example

Expeditions on the ridge number their camps upward, and Camp Five — the penultimate one below a summit pushed from Camp Six — is where the mountain decides things. Teams sleep there four hours, boil water they will not taste again for two days, and turn back or go on. Guides say you can read the whole climb in how a party arrives at Five.

Penultimate earns its place because it means exactly next to last — not "near the end," and not a grander way of saying final. Camp Six is last; Camp Five is penultimate; Camp Four is neither. The word is a precision instrument for position, and it never means "beyond ultimate," a misuse so common that using it correctly quietly signals care.

How Penultimate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

next-to-last

next-to-last: the everyday phrase for the same slot

second-to-last

second-to-last: the counting phrase for the same position

Antonyms

final

final: the very end itself

opening

opening: the first of the series

How Strong Is It? — late → penultimate → final

late vs. penultimate

late vs. penultimate: Late is the weaker marker — a late chapter sits somewhere near the end; penultimate pins it to exactly one before it.

final vs. penultimate

final vs. penultimate: Final goes further than penultimate: the final step is the end itself, one rung past the penultimate one.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pen-

Prefix — pen-: almost (Latin paene)

Root — ultim-

Root — ultim-: last, farthest

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: adjective ending

Put it together

Put it together: Pen- (almost) + ultim- (last) + -ate = almost last. Latin paene, "almost," is the same near-miss hiding in peninsula — almost an island. So the penultimate chapter is the almost-last one: the word does its counting for you, one back from the end, every time.

Use the root in a new word: ultimate

Use the root in a new word: ultimate: Her ultimate goal was the national team; every tryout before that was a step.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / precise

Penultimate is a precision word for position — next to last, no more and no less — at home in program notes, chess commentary, and syllabus week fourteen. In casual talk, next-to-last does the same work without the tuxedo. Never use it as a fancier "ultimate": it does not mean best or most, only one-from-the-end.
